activity.title: Some days just hit different. Today I got to meet my idols — Rahul Peesa , Vihaan Shringi , and Jerry Wang — at the Interlake High School Internship Fair. I've looked up to these three for a long time, and getting to talk with them in person was every bit as inspiring as I'd hoped. Even better, I got to share the moment with my friends Hongyi Ren , Ritwik Singh , and Michael C. . You never know who you'll meet or what doors a single conversation can open. Huge thanks to everyone who organized the fair — events like this make a real difference for students figuring out their next steps. #Networking #InterlakeHighSchool #InternshipFair #Grateful #Inspiration

We’re bringing the researchers behind Institute of Foundation Models ’s foundation models to Stanford. AI Valley is co-hosting an evening with the Institute of Foundation Models at MBZUAI and Stanford Society of Engineers, Scientists, and Entrepreneurs for Stanford undergrads, MS/PhD students, researchers, and technical builders. The focus is simple: how frontier foundation models move from research into real systems. We’re also excited to have Stanford faculty joining the conversation: Prof. Tengyu Ma — Stanford Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Statistics; Stanford AI Lab, working on deep learning, foundation models, and reinforcement learning Prof. James Zou — Stanford Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science, with courtesy appointments in CS and EE; HAI Faculty Affiliate Prof. Shriti Raj — Stanford HAI Faculty Fellow and Assistant Professor of Medicine, focused on human-centered health data reasoning The evening will include a technical research deep dive, a fireside conversation on model deployment, and a hands-on workshop where attendees can explore PAN, IFM’s world model platform, live. There will also be dinner, recruiting conversations, community, and giveaways for strong Q&A questions. For students and builders interested in foundation models, world models, biomedical AI, and the path from lab research to deployed systems, this should be a thoughtful room. Details and RSVP link in the comments. #Stanford #MBZUAI #FoundationModels #WorldModels #BiomedicalAI #AIResearch #AIBuilders

Building in public sounds like a string of buzzwords until it actually works for you. Three days ago I posted a reel explaining quantization. Just a concept I think is cool and stumbled upon as a part of my research for a NeuroIPS project, explained simply. It hit 35k views. But the view count is the boring part. The interesting part is who came out of the woodwork: 30 researchers inviting me to their research opportunities, students from Cornell, Stanford, and Princeton asking for advice and collaborations, a NeuroAI startup asking me to join their advisory board. None of this existed in a world where I kept the thinking private. This is the thing I wish more technical people understood: doing the work is half the job. The other half is letting people see you do it. The asymmetry is wild. A few hours of effort. A permanent piece of signal that works for you while you sleep. A network that finds you instead of the other way around. The people who win long term aren't the ones with the best ideas. They're the ones whose best ideas are visible. Reel : https://lnkd.in/gTpgJvBw

5,000+ guests. 12 high schools. Every graduating senior in IDEA San Antonio in one room. I recently had the honor of serving as the alumni speaker for IDEA Public Schools’ San Antonio College Signing Day 2026, representing every senior in the city as they revealed where they’re heading this fall. It’s hard to put into words what it meant to walk back into the community that raised me. I’m a first-gen, low-income kid who grew up on those streets, sat in those classrooms, and spent years struggling to imagine a future the world hadn’t already drawn for me. To stand on that stage as even a small piece of evidence that our futures are, in fact, ours to choose is something I’ll carry with me for the rest of my life. If I left the Class of 2026 with anything, I hope it was this: their acceptances weren’t a verdict on who they already are. They were a bet on who they’re capable of becoming — and no one in that room is more qualified than they are to make that bet pay off. To IDEA Public Schools , thank you for the trust and for the years that made all of this possible. To Destany Rainey , Nina Arrambide-Avila , and Jeff Cottrill , thank you for making this opportunity real. And a special thank you to my mentor David Robinson for refusing to let my circumstances decide the size of my future. Class of 2026 — you don’t need luck. The potential is already in you.

social interaction is dead. at least that's what everyone keeps saying in this age of ai. a few days ago i travelled with my school and some of my closest friends to Atlanta to the international career development conference. i met kids from Pennsylvania, New York, Texas, Ontario, Puerto Rico, and many more. the only thing everyone had in common was the fact that they were there. that sort of commonality seems like it wouldn't be enough to have a meaningful conversation. but that statement couldn't be more false. from meeting people who had successful ai agencies at 16 to others who seemed to have their whole life planned out, the conversations turned into exchanged contacts and laughs with people i probably won't ever see again. so going back, social interaction, is it dead? well, it being dead is a choice, not a reality. it isn't a consequence of ai or screens or whatever people seem to blame. it's a choice people make every day when they don't make the most of what exists. that's why i think social media, although frowned upon by most of our parents, at its core actually serves as an extremely important part of society. it's what kept us sane during covid and it's what's keeping us connected in this digital age. the valuable thing at that conference was not the competition it was surrounding myself with people, staying in touch with them afterwards, and creating long lasting friendships, no matter the method of communication. big things coming soon with O3O Labs (sr006) , stay tuned.

This was Stitch. He was my best friend, and he inspired me every day. 🐶 By pure luck, he found his way to my family’s home. I don’t know everything he went through before he got to us, but despite all the odds, he was one of the happiest dogs I knew. He taught me that sometimes the best thing you can do is keep pushing — and do it with a smile. Stitch was a big part of what inspired AI Valley ’s Dogathon. I hope more people get to experience the same joy, love, and companionship that he gave me. And I hope we can make life a little easier for the shelters, rescues, fosters, and volunteers working every day to give dogs like Stitch another chance. At Dogathon, you can: 🐾 Meet dogs available for adoption — and yes, you can adopt one on site 💻 Build tools for shelters, rescues, fosters, adopters, and dogs ❤️ Spend a day building something that can have a real impact For me, this one is personal. Dogathon is for Stitch, and for all the dogs still waiting to find their way home. 🐶❤️

I did not win two hackathons in four days because I was the smartest person in the room. I won because I had an amazing team willing to build something ambitious. On July 26th, my teammates Sky B. , Andrew Zhao , and I won a hackathon. Three days later, we won the Seattle AI Summit 2026 Hackathon hosted by Bloome! For our project, we built an AI agent system that streamlines home renovation and construction. One agent talks with customers to understand their vision, another analyzes company workload and available workers, another estimates costs, and another creates designs with STL files and visuals of what the renovation could look like. Within 7-10 minutes, clients can see a design, request changes, and iterate with the AI design agent in real time. The biggest takeaway was not the trophies. It was seeing how quickly a small team can turn an idea into something real. Huge shoutout to everyone who made the Seattle AI Summit 2026 such an incredible experience! Loved the conversations and insights from the Consumer AI Panel with Nancy Li Smith , Heather Jackson , Yifan Zhang , and Ke Du, MBA Also really enjoyed the fireside chat on Frontier AI Research with Yong Rui and Anna Yuan . The discussions around where AI is heading were truly inspiring. A massive thank you to the B.E.L.L.E team and Bloome (Abby Liu and Steve Shao ), for putting together such an amazing event and bringing the Seattle AI community together. Also grateful for all the amazing people I got to meet and connect with: Victor Kovalev , Dhruva Chandramohan , Michael Andres Diaz Moreira , Wesley Richards , Senthil Arun , Nigel Sharp 🚂 , Arjun Harsha , Rahul Peesa , Fuad Abdella , Vedansh Anand , Ridwan Grimes , Khalid M. , Elva(Jiani) He , Abhinav Bandaru and many more. Thank you Sky B. and Andrew Zhao for building this with me. Two hackathons. Four days. One incredible team.

I was initially rejected from Y Combinator startup school. Found out I was accepted on Monday. To preface, The bay area last year more than changed my life, and I really regretted missing the application for yc sus 2025, so I was looking forward to sus 2026. To reconnecting with some friends and welcoming the incoming batch of new builders to the bay. So to say the rejection didn’t bother me would be an understatement. It stung — just not quite as deeply as it once would have. You might think you are doing everything right: Early startup experience both large and personal. Top cs degrees. A great operator network. An unwavering fire to keep showing up. Keep working. To create something meaningful. And still, the outcome may be a bit silly 🤪 Common life lesson that still never feels easy: effort does not guarantee recognition, and talent does not make us immune to rejection. So passion has to become the reason. When you care deeply enough about the work, the doors that open and close begin to matter less. Don’t get me wrong rejections still hurt, but you keep building because you cannot imagine doing anything else. You follow the path because it feels true to you, even when no one is watching and nothing is promised — expectations and reality become secondary. Celebrate when the door opens. Keep moving when it does not. Do not wait for the world to validate what already makes you feel alive. You are the author of your own life. And all your rejections and setbacks will start to sting a bit less.

I had my hand up for the entire 45 minutes when I met Vinod Khosla trying to ask him this As my buddy Pavan Kumar and I walked to Khosla with no invite and no idea if we would be let in, we argued about how humility is the single biggest lever to how fast you grow We got in. Sat down with our notebooks out, preemptive questions jotted down, and ready to learn as much as possible from one of the greatest tech visionaries around. Oh and here's all my learnings from listening to him But here's the question I never got to ask him: "Where do you place the equilibrium between past accolades and current success in a founding journey?” So the people who’ve been doing this far longer than I have, where do you see this equilibrium?

One month ago, this startup was just an idea. Today, the codebase spans nearly 2,000 unique files—with Rust at its core and a growing stack across JavaScript, Python, HTML, and more. And somehow, I’ve been building it while: • Attending BU RISE, one of the most rigorous summer research programs • Working through college applications and essays • Learning how to turn an ambitious idea into a real product None of this progress would have been possible without my incredible team. Grateful to Ritwik Singh , Hongyi Ren , and Eric Wang for being such outstanding teammates and helping turn our startup vision into reality. Thank you all for believing in the vision, challenging ideas, solving hard problems, and continuing to show up. I’m genuinely grateful to be building alongside you. It hasn’t meant perfect balance. It has meant late nights, difficult tradeoffs, constant debugging, and moving forward even when progress felt slow. There’s still a long way to go, but seeing one month of work become something tangible is incredibly motivating. More soon. 🚀 #Startup #BuildingInPublic #Entrepreneurship #SoftwareEngineering #BURISE #StudentFounder
